scope: Post-inspection development regression. Stored responses to older prompts are fixtures, not valid provider replay/new model assessments. Original fixed score unchanged.

unresolved_concerns: cart_id is included as a predictive feature because feats() excludes only 'event', allowing the tree to memorize or exploit arbitrary numeric cart identifiers and imposing an unjustified ordinal structure on them.

The row-wise stratified train_test_split does not group by cart_id, so records from the same cart can appear in both training and test sets; this leaks cart-specific information and overstates performance for previously unseen carts.

The deployment population is unresolved: performance on records from already represented carts and performance on records from unseen carts require different partitions, so an unconditional generalization claim is unsupported.
Evaluation relies on a single 25% split (about 30 test records from 120 rows), giving high sampling variance with no repeated splits, cross-validation, confidence interval, or uncertainty assessment.
Accuracy is reported alone with no baseline, per-class errors, calibration, or grouped/unseen-cart analysis; the balanced 0.5 prevalence in the supplied data may also not match deployment prevalence.
Temporal/target leakage: feats() uses every column except 'event', so it includes downstream_status as a predictor.

downstream_status is produced after the final acceptance test and records its outcome, but the intended decision is screening before that test; it is unavailable at decision time and may proxy the outcome.
The reported cross-validated accuracy therefore does not estimate performance achievable using only the available mix_* features and cannot support the intended pre-test screening conclusion.
The feature-selection rule is indiscriminate: any future or post-decision column present in the CSV would automatically be included.

verification_index availability at the acceptance decision is undocumented: it may be a subsequent verification measurement rather than an intake measurement, creating potential post-decision/target leakage.
feats() automatically includes every non-target column, so verification_index is used without any availability or temporal-validity check.
The cross-validated accuracy therefore may measure retrospective prediction using information unavailable when screening, rather than performance achievable at acceptance.
No feature-exclusion, temporal-cutoff, or sensitivity analysis without verification_index is supplied to bound the possible leakage effect.
The 120-row, single-seed 3-fold accuracy estimate is also limited for screening conclusions, with no uncertainty, calibration, threshold, or error-cost assessment.

summary.interval_note: Unpaired row bootstrap, conditional on fixed predictions; all seeds must agree for an inflation verdict.
